Areas of complex need (five areas of work) ::: areas of complex need|areas of work|five areas ::: local-programme ::: South Tees Delivery Plan (Version 2); MHCLG (2020) Changing Futures Prospectus (cohort definition). :::  ::: The five overlapping areas of need that define who the programme works with: criminal justice, mental health, homelessness, domestic abuse and substance use. In South Tees a person must be in contact with two or more of these to access the service (South Tees Delivery Plan); the national Changing Futures cohort (MHCLG 2020 Prospectus) is defined more narrowly as three or more. CAPVA ::: CAPVA ::: substantive ::: Tees Child Protection Partnership — Child to Parent Violence and Abuse guidance; the national concept is set out in the Home Office (2015) Information guide: Adolescent to Parent Violence and Abuse (https://www.teescpp.org.uk/procedures-and-guidance-on-specific-issues-that-affect-children/child-to-parent-violence-and-abuse/) :::  ::: Abuse perpetrated by a child or adolescent against a parent or carer. The broader clinical convention (Royal College of Emergency Medicine) is five or more attendances in a year. A threshold, not a label for the person. :::  ::: Frequent attender

The National Lottery Community Fund (TNLCF) ::: The National Lottery Community Fund|National Lottery Community Fund|TNLCF|Big Lottery Fund ::: statutory ::: National Lottery Act 2006 (established the Big Lottery Fund, which has operated as The National Lottery Community Fund since 2019). (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2006/23/contents) :::  ::: The operating name since 2019 of the Big Lottery Fund: the UK's largest funder of community activity, distributing money raised for good causes by National Lottery players. Joint funder of Changing Futures with MHCLG. ::: TNLCF ::: The National Lottery Community Fund
The system ::: the system ::: substantive ::: Working definition adopted in this deep-dive series. :::  ::: All the services around a person — health, housing, social care, justice, substance use, domestic abuse and welfare, whether statutory, commissioned or voluntary-sector — seen from the person's point of view rather than any one agency's. The related principle is that the system should adapt to the person, not the person to the system. :::  ::: The system
Thrive Partnership ::: Thrive Partnership|THRIVE|Thrive ::: local-programme ::: We Are With You — the Thrive Partnership (Redcar and Cleveland; England's first integrated Domestic Abuse and Substance Use model); Thrive Impact Report 2024–2025 (https://www.wearewithyou.org.uk/latest/news-and-views/women-stronger-together-a-three-way-conversation-with-the-thrive-partnership) :::  ::: The Redcar and Cleveland partnership delivering England's first integrated Domestic Abuse and Substance Use (IDAS) service model: collaborative, trauma-informed support. THRIVE stands for Trusting, Hopeful, Resilient, Involved, Valued and Empowered. Partners: We Are With You (drug and alcohol support), Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council, Harbour Support Services (domestic abuse), Recovery Connections and Intuitive Thinking Skills. ::: THRIVE ::: Thrive Partnership

TIPC ::: TIPC|Trauma-Informed Practice Co-ordinator|Trauma-Informed Practice Coordinator ::: local-programme ::: South Tees Changing Futures — Trauma-Informed Practice workstream (programme role). :::  ::: The named South Tees Changing Futures role responsible for running the Trauma-Informed Practice workstream. ::: TIPC ::: Trauma-Informed Practice Co-ordinator
Trauma-aware / -curious / -informed / -responsive ::: TRAUMA-AWARE ::: local-programme ::: South Tees Changing Futures programme — the local trauma-informed maturity framework (four developmental phases). :::  ::: The four developmental phases in the South Tees framework. An organisation is trauma-responsive when Trauma-informed practice (TIP) is the norm and no longer dependent on champions. No South Tees organisation in the evidence base has reached this phase. :::  ::: Trauma-aware / -curious / -informed / -responsive
Trauma-informed care (TIC) ::: TIC ::: substantive ::: SAMHSA (2014) SAMHSA's Concept of Trauma and Guidance for a Trauma-Informed Approach. Rockville, MD: SAMHSA. :::  ::: Retained only when quoting source documents that use 'care' rather than 'practice'; the series uses trauma-informed practice (TIP) by default. ::: TIC ::: Trauma-informed care
Trauma-Informed Champion ::: champion|TIP champion|Trauma-Informed Champion ::: local-programme ::: Trauma-Informed Champions Charter (South Tees; funded through Changing Futures). :::  ::: A trained practitioner who has committed, via the Trauma-Informed Champions Charter, to embedding trauma-informed practice within their employing organisation. South Tees identified 67 named champions across 11 services. :::  ::: Trauma-Informed Champion
Trauma-Informed Champions Charter ::: Charter|Champions Charter ::: local-programme ::: Trauma-Informed Champions Charter (South Tees; funded through Changing Futures). :::  ::: South Tees's local commitment to trauma-informed practice, funded through Changing Futures. It asks every service to recognise the impact of trauma and respond with kindness and compassion, built on six principles: safety; trust and transparency; choice and voice; collaboration; empowerment; and inclusivity. :::  ::: Trauma-Informed Champions Charter
Trauma-informed practice (TIP) ::: trauma-informed practice|TIP ::: substantive ::: OHID (2022) Working definition of trauma-informed practice (GOV.UK) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/working-definition-of-trauma-informed-practice/working-definition-of-trauma-informed-practice) :::  ::: A whole-system approach to realising the prevalence of trauma, recognising its effects, responding by embedding that knowledge in practice, and resisting re-traumatisation. The series adopts the Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID) (2022) England working definition, with Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)'s (2014) four assumptions and six principles as the underlying framework. ::: TIP ::: Trauma-informed practice

Vicarious trauma ::: Vicarious trauma|Vicarious traumatisation|Vicarious traumatization|VT ::: substantive ::: McCann, I.L. and Pearlman, L.A. (1990) Vicarious traumatisation: a framework for understanding the psychological effects of working with victims. :::  ::: Vicarious trauma (vicarious traumatisation) — the cumulative, gradual transformation in a worker's own inner experience and worldview that results from empathic engagement with trauma survivors over time. :::  ::: Vicarious trauma
Victims and Prisoners Act 2024 ::: VICTIMS ::: local-programme ::: Victims and Prisoners Act 2024 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2024/21/contents) :::  ::: Creates a statutory duty for local authorities, OPCCs and ICBs to collaborate on commissioning Domestic abuse (DA), sexual abuse and serious violence support, from April 2026. :::  ::: Victims and Prisoners Act 2024

WAWY (We Are With You) ::: WAWY|We Are With You ::: organisation :::  ::: findthatcharity org ID GB-CHC-1001957 (https://findthatcharity.uk/orgid/GB-CHC-1001957) ::: We Are With You (formerly Addaction) — the commissioned substance-use service across Redcar & Cleveland. ::: WAWY ::: We Are With You
Workstream ::: workstream ::: local-programme ::: South Tees Delivery Plan (Version 2); STCFP Board Terms of Reference. :::  ::: One of the strands the programme is organised into. The Delivery Plan sets out six: a governance strand (Programme Management and Ideas Factory) and five delivery strands — Enhanced Case Management, Innovation Fund, Key Worker Support, VCS Infrastructure, and Embedding Trauma-Informed Services. Workstreams are how the programme delivers, as distinct from the five areas of complex need that define who it works with. :::  ::: Workstream
